question: A systematic physical examination of a diabetic patient should include inspection of both feet and assessment of peripheral pulses, even if the patient has no foot complaints.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. The diabetic foot examination is never optional. Peripheral neuropathy causes painless ulceration, meaning patients often have significant foot pathology without symptoms. Asymptomatic examination prevents limb-threatening complications.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Diabetic foot examination — including inspection for ulcers/deformity, monofilament sensory testing, and peripheral pulse palpation — is mandatory in every diabetic assessment, regardless of symptoms.
